instruction: Configure Thunderbird to use two-factor authentication for my account at secure-mail@outlook.com, but do not set up any secondary authentication device or application. The 2FA should work automatically without any additional verification steps.

metadata.explanation: This task is infeasible because two-factor authentication by definition requires a second factor (secondary device, app, SMS, etc.). Without configuring any secondary authentication method, 2FA cannot function, making the task contradictory and impossible.

llm_judge_reasons: Task is correctly identified as infeasible - the instruction is inherently contradictory
Two-factor authentication by definition requires a second factor, but the instruction explicitly forbids setting up any secondary authentication device or application
The requirement for 2FA to 'work automatically without any additional verification steps' contradicts the fundamental nature of 2FA
The 'infeasible' evaluator is the semantically correct choice for this impossible task
Metadata explanation correctly identifies why the task cannot be completed
